The homepage is dying. No two serious buyers should still be seeing the same website...

AI made per-account personalization basically free. Which means a website that speaks San Francisco to a buyer sitting in Madrid isn't neutral anymore… it's a choice.

That was take one of many at today's growth coffee with Emilio Bujosa from Supersonik, where we dug into B2B marketing in the AI era.

Quick context, because you should know them: Supersonik builds AI agents that give live, personalized demos of your product, every buyer gets a 1:1 walkthrough, any hour, any language. While everyone else builds agents that replace people, they built one that explains things to people.

It's the kind of product where you go "wait, why doesn't every B2B company have this yet?"

(also yes, two gingers in one growth conversation. that's 0.1% of the population)

The rest of the playbook we discussed:
✨ Nobody cares what feature you shipped. They care which annoying thing it kills. Every launch should start with the pain, not the product.
✨ B2B marketing has a courage problem, not a budget problem. One weird idea outperforms a quarter of safe ones.
✨ And the hill I'll die on: your growth person is the journalist of your company. Not "we were at this event." Why should a stranger care that you were?

Great products still lose to louder ones. The winners of the next few years will treat distribution as part of the product.

Supersonik, remember the name. 👀

And Barcelona startups, I just moved here, and this is my favorite way to meet you.
If you're building something interesting and want a growth coffee, my DMs are open. ☕
